inspection_outcome: Five established findings: one Major proof-dependency defect and four Minor local corrections.
summary: The stated principal-triple slice is not surjective in permitted characteristics, including the sufficient prime range used downstream. Four local cohomology, root-sign, site and prime-set statements require correction. Main moduli-space conclusions are not thereby shown false.

problems.title: The principal-triple slice is not surjective in permitted characteristics
problems.claim: X -> F+X from g^E to g//G is an isomorphism for simple adjoint G and ell not dividing |W|.
problems.assumptions: L algebraically closed, G=PGL5, ell=7, q=3, trivial action; |W|=120, h=5, ord_7(3)=6. Principal triple E=Jordan5, F subdiagonal(4,6,6,4), H=diag(4,2,0,-2,-4).
problems.check_method: Root reconstructed matrix relations, polynomial centralizer and invariant trace argument; exact arithmetic and independent 4x4 determinant computation. Helper C2 and PGL5 candidates separately attributed; root originated PGL4 extension.
problems.decisive_evidence: g^E=span(E,E^2,E^3,E^4). For Y=F+xE+yE^2+zE^3+wE^4, tr(Y^3)=3y(24+36+24)=252y=0 mod7. D=diag(1,1,-2,0,0) has tr(D^3)=-6=1 mod7. Thus the invariant vanishes on the entire slice but not on the quotient. PGL4 ell5 similarly tr(Y^2)=20x=0. C2 ell3 also falsifies regularity of H and its slice has determinant0.
problems.result: Exact counterexample to the stated intermediate isomorphism, including the body ell>h and sufficient chi-star(q) range.
problems.counterevidence: B.5 final determinant formula holds in all three explicit examples by centralizer weights. No counterexample to main moduli flatness, connectedness, B.5 final identity or Theorem5.7 established. Veldkamp uses its specified Chevalley sums, not automatically the principal F used here.
problems.impact: The displayed section-based derivation of the graded equivariant centralizer identity used for unobstructedness requires substantive repair.

correction.statement: Give a valid characteristic-sensitive equivariant centralizer argument or correctly chosen section. Neither ell>h nor existing banal sufficient exclusions repairs the specified slice.
correction.verification: Example-specific determinant formulas verified; general replacement proof not established.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: PGL5 over algebraically closed characteristic7, 7 does not divide120, and7>h5. E has one regular Jordan block; trace-zero centralizer is span E through E4 because5 is invertible. The displayed F,H satisfy the sl2 relations.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: A diagonal term in (F+xE+yE2+zE3+wE4)^3 requires precisely two F and one yE2; its trace is3y(24+36+24)=252y=0 modulo7. The invariant tr(D3) for traceless D=diag(1,1,-2,0,0) equals1 modulo7. Hence the specified slice misses quotient values. PGL4 characteristic5 and C2 characteristic3 checks independently reconstruct the stated additional obstructions.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_impact: Actual AppendixB.4 asserts this precise principal-triple map under only ell not dividing the Weyl order, and p60 explicitly invokes B.5 in Proposition5.18. Actual Veldkamp pp232,234?235 uses specified Chevalley sums X+ and X-, so it does not identify this F-based section. Centralizer weights directly reproduce B.5's determinant in these examples; no failure of that identity or main moduli theorem established.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_check: A characteristic-sensitive equivariant centralizer proof or correctly chosen equivariant section is still needed. Neither ell>h nor the stated sufficient prime condition cures the exact PGL5 slice; no general repair has been certified.

problems.title: The full inertia H1 vanishing assertion is false
problems.claim: H1(I_F,T(L))=1 because the action factors through a cyclic ell-group and T(L) is uniquely ell-divisible.
problems.assumptions: p2, ell3, T=Gm, L=Fbar3, trivial action.
problems.check_method: Explicit continuous tame character and direct coboundary calculation.
problems.decisive_evidence: I_F surjects onto C5 and C5 embeds in mu5(L); the resulting nontrivial continuous cocycle is not a coboundary for trivial action.
problems.result: The literal full-inertia group is too large.
problems.counterevidence: The fixed-component obstruction factors through finite cyclic ell-group C. H1(C,T(L))=0 by invertibility of |C| on T(L), so the intended lifting can be repaired.
problems.impact: Local cohomology statement and justification require restriction; Cor4.20 not refuted.

correction.statement: Use H1(C,T(L)), or cocycles through I_F/I_F^ell, for the relevant obstruction.
correction.verification: Finite-group averaging/unique divisibility verified for that restricted action.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: p2,ell3,algebraically closed F3, split Gm with trivial action; continuous tame quotient C5 exists and mu5 is nontrivial.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: The nonzero tame character is a continuous1-cocycle and cannot be a coboundary for trivial action. Source43 really writes full H1(IF,T(L)), not the quotient used on44.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_impact: The actual component obstruction factors through the finite ell-action; uniquely ell-divisible T(L) kills cohomology of that finite quotient. The unnecessarily broad vanishing statement is false, whereas its restricted local use can be retained. Corollary4.20 not refuted.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_check: Restrict cohomology to the finite cyclic ell-action or the indicated pro-ell quotient with continuous discrete torsion coefficients. Do not claim full-inertia vanishing.

problems.title: The finite-image adjustment uses the wrong root sign
problems.claim: Choose t^r=g^r and multiply the Frobenius value g by t to obtain finite image.
problems.assumptions: G=Gm, trivial action, phi(s)=1, phi(Fr)=2 over Qbar.
problems.check_method: Direct rank-one counterexample; commuting inverse-root repair.
problems.decisive_evidence: t=2*zeta for zeta^r=1 gives new Frobenius value4*zeta of infinite order.
problems.counterevidence: Choose r so g^r lies in identity component of the g-fixed inertia torus, then t^r=g^-r in that torus. It commutes with g and (tg)^r=1; same connected component preserved.
problems.impact: Local proof step only; existence lemma not refuted.

correction.statement: Use a commuting inverse root in (U^Adg)^0 after increasing r.
correction.verification: Algebraic power calculation and connected torus argument checked.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: Trivial torus over Qbar, trivial inertia, Frobenius2 satisfies the semisimple rank-one setup.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: The source defines multiplication by t then chooses t^r=g^r. This gives t=2zeta and new Frobenius4zeta, of infinite order.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_impact: Taking the inverse root in the identity component of the g-fixed inertia torus after enlarging r makes t commute with g and (tg)^r=1. This keeps the connected component. The local printed adjustment fails; existence conclusion is not disproved.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_check: Commutation and identity-component membership are necessary parts of the inverse-root correction, and are retained in the report.

problems.title: Central-isogeny exactness is asserted on the wrong site
problems.claim: The displayed fixed-point/cohomology sequence is exact on the big etale site for all allowed central isogenies.
problems.assumptions: R=Z[1/3], Gamma=C3 trivial action, SL2->PGL2 with kernel mu2. A=F2[u,u^-1].
problems.check_method: Explicit central isogeny and lifting obstruction at the generic point.
problems.decisive_evidence: H1(C3,mu2)=1, but class diag(u,1) cannot lift etale-locally to SL2: it requires a^2u=1 and a purely inseparable square root over F2(u).
problems.result: The stated etale sheaf epimorphism/exactness fails.
problems.counterevidence: Central isogeny is fppf-surjective; finite etale component sheaves can then be handled in the etale topology. A.11/A.12 conclusions not refuted.
problems.impact: Site and descent argument must be corrected without assuming isogeny degree invertible from |Gamma| invertible.

correction.statement: Form the central-isogeny sequence fppf-locally, then descend finite etale component groups.
correction.verification: Obstruction and availability of fppf square-root cover checked; not a full new proof of all Appendix A.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: R=Z[1/3],Gamma=C3 with trivial action, reductive SL2 and PGL2,central kernelmu2; only |Gamma| is required invertible.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: H1(C3,mu2) is trivial, but diag(u,1) in PGL2(F2[u,u^-1]) requires a square root of u^-1 to lift to SL2. At F2(u) this is purely inseparable and cannot be supplied by an etale extension, so the source92 big-etale exactness is false.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_impact: The fppf square-root cover supplies the intended lift. Finite etale component-group descent is a distinct later step; no counterexample to A.11's final finiteness statement is given.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_check: The proposed change of site is a valid local repair route, not a certified fresh proof of all AppendixA.

problems.title: The introductory prime exclusions are reversed
problems.claim: Positive M divisible by all LG-banal primes or their product.
problems.assumptions: Banal primes form a cofinite set; q2 trivial-action Gm gives all ell !=2.
problems.check_method: Quantifier check plus explicit torus model and comparison to formal theorem.
problems.decisive_evidence: No positive integer can be divisible by infinitely many distinct primes; formal Prop6.2 correctly inverts N_G and non-banal primes.
problems.counterevidence: Section6 formal localization statement has the correct finite exclusions.
problems.impact: Local introductory wording, not formal GIT result.

correction.statement: Replace by non-banal, retaining N_G condition and unramified refinement.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: Source9 defines LG-banal primes as the complement of a finite set; source10 calls for a positive integer divisible by all of them.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_check: No positive integer has all primes in an infinite cofinite set as divisors. Source73 Proposition6.2 instead correctly inverts NG and non-banal primes; Remark6.3 supplies the unramified refinement.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_impact: This is restricted to two introductory descriptions of the prime set. The formal GIT localization theorem uses the correct set.
independent_acceptance_check.repair_check: Replace banal by non-banal while retaining the separate NG requirement and unramified qualification.

clarifications: Lemma4.28's finite-action argument can use an abstract infinite cyclic group; full inertia is not procyclic. This is not entered as a separate theorem counterexample.
The final B5 determinant identity holds in all explicit examples; a failed proof step is distinguished from a false final identity.
A proposed blanket ell>h repair was rejected after exact PGL4 and PGL5 checks. No full replacement theorem is certified.

Complete external dependencies and exceptional tables not independently rederived
